newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Salomon Bros sees gains in LatAm steel sector.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Bros sees gains in LatAm steel sector.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said the Latin American steel sector should post stronger net earnings for the second half of 1996 compared with the first six months.
In a statement made available in Brasilia, Salomon said the net profits of Brazil's Cosipa and Argentina's Acindar should improve as a result.

"The Latin American steel sector should post stronger net earnings for the second half..., largely because of an expected recovery in Brazilian and Argentine steel shipments," said the firm's Latin American mining and steel analyst Mauricio Reveco.

The statement said that according to the firm's new quarterly report, major Latin American steel producers' net profit reached $452 million in the first half of 1996, a drop of 23 percent on the first half of 1995.
"This decrease largely reflects heavy restructuring costs at Cosipa and Acindar, partially offset by the excellent results posted by Ahmsa and Hylsamex," it said.
It added, "Salomon remains positive over the future performance of the Mexican steel sector. Record-level production is forecast for 1996."
Salomon also said the Brazilian steel industry, operating in a difficult environment, continues to gather strength.
The analyst said "results for the second half of 1996 likely will improve...and will demonstrate greater efficiency gains."
Salomon said the Argentine steel sector was exceeding analysts' expectations.
"Steel making in Latin America is an industry with strong upside potential in terms of revenue and profitability," Salomon analyst Harald Liberge said in the statement.
"We expect it to continue to outperform the Latin American market over the next two years."
